study.question: Do previous-advertisement IDs improve full-population validation click AUC conditional on all remaining aligned history fields, actions, task masks, supplied order and unchanged current-target IDs in the strongest visible model, at measured cost?
study.hypothesis: The imported full-ID model may use historical advertisement identity or recurrence beyond the remaining fields. Removing both embedded historical ID values and exact-ID match evidence will reduce click AUC if that information is useful under this frozen implementation. A frequency-weighted bag of historical ID embeddings plus the target-ID repeat count may recover the gain without event-level ID alignment. This is a conditional predictive-utility study, not a new architecture claim or evidence of a behavioral causal mechanism.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit the strongest visible source byte-for-byte for full use. In two standalone copies intervene only at historical ID embeddings and exact-ID equality evidence; preserve all other forward/learning machinery including the nonstandard surrogate VJP. Imported result does not contain an identity ablation.

Archived v4 primary text lines 219-277 describes concatenated item-field embeddings, target-conditioned local activation and unnormalized weighted pooling; lines 232-240 describe unordered sum/average pooling. These are inherited/reference components. The proposed difference is a conditional advertisement-ID information ablation in the imported four-task model, not a claim to invent attention or bag pooling.

Only the pinned author README is available/read (lines 4-8), explicitly warning that its behavior dataset has category, brand and behavior type but no item. It cannot establish the value or semantics of historical advertisement IDs in this released impression-history benchmark. Publisher full paper remains unavailable; no detailed DMR reproduction or priority claim.

Cached primary section 2.3 lists unified interaction alternatives including EST and HyFormer. Their description does not isolate historical-ID utility. No architecture from those cards is adopted in this single-factor information study.

study.proposed_difference: Use three standalone modules. Full candidate.py remains byte-identical to the imported source. Blind replaces only the historical item_id embedding slice with zeros and forces the item_id column of exact-match membership/counts to zero before affinity, union and support construction. Counts-only replaces that slice with its validity-masked FP32 mean embedding broadcast identically to each valid slot; retains log1p of the masked number of target-ID matches in the existing count coordinate; and forces all event-level item_id match membership to zero before affinity, union and support. Category/brand match computation is unchanged. Target embeddings are concatenated from the untouched final slot. No parameters, state buffers, RNG calls or losses are added; no event is dropped or reordered. Counts-only means a compressed unordered ID frequency representation, not exact storage of the complete count vector.
predictions: Primary paired contrast: delta_identity=AUC(full)-AUC(blind)>0 if conditional identity information improves the inherited implementation. Record the signed difference even when negative or null.

If unordered identity frequencies are sufficient for the observed gain, counts-only will recover most of delta_identity. Predeclare practical equivalence as abs(AUC(full)-AUC(counts-only))<=0.0002; this descriptive margin is not a significance test.

If full exceeds blind but counts-only is substantially worse than full, aligned access is provisionally useful for these encodings, with the finite bag bottleneck and normalization/optimization changes retained as alternatives.

All variants are expected to have 32192421 total parameters (31793216 embeddings and 399205 dense), zero added parameters. Remeasure rather than assume. No speedup is predicted: blind still performs the original shared lookup, and counts adds a reduction.

At identical initialized state, blind predictions are invariant to any in-range historical-ID replacement that leaves target IDs, other fields and masks fixed. Counts-only is invariant within floating-point tolerance to permuting IDs among valid historical slots, independently of other aligned fields. Masked history perturbations and empty histories cannot contribute ID information.
falsifiers: Full AUC no greater than blind provides no support for useful conditional historical-ID information under the frozen recipe; do not reinterpret the imported full-versus-DIN gain as ID evidence.
Counts-only practically matching full weakens the event-alignment explanation. A counts-only failure alone cannot refute unordered identity utility because this mean embedding is lossy.
A gain explained by unequal exposure, extra learned capacity, input/mask leakage, inability to reproduce full, or unjustified measured cost fails the intended conditional-utility claim.

Any blind response to historical-ID-only replacement, counts-only response beyond numerical tolerance to valid-slot ID permutation, masked-ID contribution, changed target embeddings, unequal learned-state shapes, nonfinite outputs/gradients or unexpected parameters invalidates that implementation contrast.
alternative_explanations: One frozen seed is preliminary; repeated samples from a user are dependent and cannot be treated as independent experimental repetitions.

Parameter counts and tensor widths are matched, but removing information necessarily changes effective representation rank, sparse embedding updates, learned normalizer states and optimization trajectory.
Counts-only uses a finite-width mean embedding plus target recurrence count; it can lose multiset distinctions. Full greater than counts-only does not uniquely establish event-alignment utility.
Historical IDs can be inferred in part from the retained aligned item fields. A null conditional effect does not show unconditional irrelevance.
Inherited offline feedback visibility, whole-window vocabulary/static snapshots and surrogate context backward limit causal/production interpretation.

Exact-ID equality also influences the inherited normalizer support during training; removing this ID-derived information changes that support without changing the normalizer algorithm. This is part of the total ID-access intervention, not attribution to embeddings alone.

Full/ID-blind differences may depend on target/history sharing of the embedding table, target recurrence, identity popularity, gradients or regularization; the suite does not separately identify those mechanisms.
History-length slices are exploratory effect localization; histories and identity exposure correlate. Do not infer a temporal behavior mechanism from those slices.
